title: Secretary of State of Vermont

context.text: Vermont elects its Secretary of State to a two-year term. Incumbent Sarah Copeland Hanzas is seeking a third term.
Vermont's town and city clerks run local elections; the Secretary of State's office supports them and maintains the statewide election-management system.

candidates.name: Sarah Copeland Hanzas
candidates.ballotNote: Renominated in the August 11 Democratic primary.
candidates.currentRole: Secretary of State of Vermont (since January 2023)

summary.text: Sarah Copeland Hanzas is the incumbent Democratic Secretary of State, seeking a third two-year term. Before her election in 2022 she served nearly two decades in the Vermont House. In office she has overseen replacement of the state's election-management IT systems and civic-education programs, and she and the Attorney General won dismissal of a Department of Justice suit demanding Vermont's unredacted voter list.

background.text: Served in the Vermont House of Representatives for nearly two decades before becoming Secretary of State; lives in Bradford.
First elected Secretary of State in 2022 and re-elected in 2024.

priorities.text: Civic education, including the Kid Governor program (classrooms in all 14 counties this year) and Vermont Civic Connect, a partnership with businesses and nonprofits offering employers a toolkit on how, where and when to vote.
Election administration: completing the replacement of aging IT systems and, per her interview, a closer collaboration with the Department of Motor Vehicles on voter-registration data transfers.

positions.summary: Asked in a Vermont Public interview whether a state law like the SAVE Act, requiring proof of citizenship to register, would benefit Vermont, she said she did not see a benefit.
positions.quote: it would have the effect of making it harder for a lot of people who have been voters their whole life to be able to vote

record.text: With Attorney General Charity Clark, issued a joint statement after a federal judge dismissed on September 17, 2026 the Department of Justice's lawsuit demanding Vermont's unredacted voter list; the Secretary said Vermont law bars sharing the full voter file with the federal government.

With Governor Phil Scott, announced in August 2026 that the state had removed nearly 900 people from the voter rolls who had been registered through the Department of Motor Vehicles without intending to register; she said none of them had voted.
Said that the 2026 primary results were processed on a new election-management computer system without the snags of 2022 and 2024.

candidates.name: H. Brooke Paige
candidates.ballotNote: Won the Republican primary for Secretary of State (and for three other statewide offices); withdrew from the other three and remains on the ballot for this one.

summary.text: H. Brooke Paige of Washington, Vermont, is the Republican nominee for Secretary of State. He first ran for statewide office in 2012 and says this is about his fifth run for the office. In 2026 he entered Republican primaries for four statewide offices, then withdrew from three after being certified the winner.

background.text: Is a justice of the peace in his town and serves on its board of civil authority; says he has filed several lawsuits against the Secretary of State over election matters.

priorities.text: Moving ballot-counting and election results away from the Secretary of State toward town boards of civil authority, which he says is the model in the Vermont Constitution.
Asked what he would do differently from the current Secretary of State, he said: "I would follow the Constitution."

Argues the Secretary of State has a conflict of interest in counting ballots for races in which the Secretary is a candidate: "The Secretary of State should not be involved in the counting of the ballots."

candidates.researchNotes: Paige was asked about election-administration structure, not about proof of citizenship, so no statement on that issue is recorded; no campaign website for him was reviewed.

candidates.name: Rachel Shaw
candidates.ballotNote: Nominated by the Vermont Progressive Party.

summary.text: Rachel Shaw of Bennington is the Progressive Party nominee for Secretary of State. Little public information about her campaign for this office was found.

candidates.researchNotes: No campaign website or questionnaire response for the Secretary of State race was found; Vermont Public reported multiple unsuccessful attempts to reach her.

researchNotes: Slate: Vermont Secretary of State's 2026 general-election qualified-candidates file lists Hanzas (D), Paige (R) and Shaw (Progressive), consistent with Vermont Public and WCAX reporting. Paige's status: he withdrew only from the attorney general, auditor and treasurer nominations. Shaw is tiered minimal and the Progressive Party's last statewide share was not checked; Hanzas's only documented stance on a listed issue is her interview answer on proof of citizenship.
